The clearest sign of a failed AI redesign is a manager spending all day copying context between machines.

This is the Human Middleware Manager. Strategy becomes their prompt. Agent output becomes their summary. Judgment becomes an approval queue. Their calendar fills with handoffs, but they rarely author doctrine or confront customers, operations, and consequences.

The problem is not the manager. It is the architecture. The organization added a new source of cognition without redesigning how intent reaches action. It bolted the dynamo to the line shaft, then kept people in place as belts and pulleys.

People should author doctrine and expose it to reality. Doctrine should carry intent to agents.

Leave the old architecture intact, and every new agent creates more translation, supervision, and contradiction—until your highest-paid people are moving context instead of moving the company.

novel_idea.topic_thesis: In an AI-native organization, people should author doctrine and confront reality—not serve as middleware carrying context between agents.
novel_idea.angle: Diagnose the human-middleware pattern through managers who spend their time translating strategy into prompts, approvals, summaries, and handoffs. Show that the underlying problem is architectural: the organization has added a new source of cognition without redesigning how intent reaches action.
novel_idea.hook: If your managers spend all day copying strategy into prompts, approvals, and summaries, you did not redesign work for AI. You electrified the line shaft.
novel_idea.argument_summary: Traditional organizations used managers, meetings, and specialists to distribute scarce cognition and context. AI makes much execution cheap, but many firms preserve the old architecture by keeping people as relay nodes between strategy and agents. That retains delay, adds transmission loss, and leaves every executing unit dependent on private interpretation. The alternative is not removing people. It is moving them into the functions the source says remain essential: authoring doctrine, exercising taste and moral accountability, confronting customers and other boundaries of consequence, and updating doctrine when reality contradicts it. Canonical, current, bounded doctrine should carry intent into execution; humans should govern the map and absorb reality rather than manually retransmit instructions.
novel_idea.novelty_rationale: The closest prior post argued that the One-Man Job reduces coordination while eroding the social contact that once generated trust. This argument addresses a different mechanism and operator decision: firms preserve obsolete coordination architecture by using people as context relays after cognition becomes cheap. Its consequence is transmission loss and an Auteur bottleneck, not social atomization. Its prescription is to make doctrine the middleware while reserving people for authorship, reality-contact, accountability, and repair.
novel_idea.source_grounding: The source explicitly states, “People should not be the middleware. Doctrine should be the middleware,” while preserving human roles in taste, legal and moral accountability, trust, grief, and repair. “Auteurs, Agents, Actors” assigns doctrine authorship to Auteurs, doctrine execution to Agents, and boundary-of-consequence reality contact to Actors. “The Dynamo and the Agent” grounds the line-shaft analogy: early adopters installed new power inside old layouts, while the deeper gains required redesign around the new bottleneck.

payload.body_text:
Monday morning is where honest conclusions go to die.

Friday’s Crossing rejects a core pricing premise. By 9 a.m. Monday, the sales prompt still makes the old promise, the dashboard rewards it, and the approval rules permit it. The team changed its mind. The operating system did not.

A Crossing should not close at recognition. It closes when the verdict is encoded into doctrine and propagated to every affected human and machine workflow.

Do not run this move when junior people cannot safely contradict senior people. Lower the stakes and build trust first.

Closing checklist:

1. Record the verdict, owner, effective date, and what evidence would reverse it.
2. Update doctrine, prompts, permissions, evaluations, dashboards, and decision rules.
3. Identify every affected person, agent, workflow, and external commitment; confirm receipt.
4. Delete the rejected premise and test execution at the boundary where reality answers.

If the old premise can still execute on Monday, the Crossing is still open.

novel_idea.topic_thesis: A Crossing should not close until its verdict has been encoded into doctrine and propagated to every affected human and machine workflow.
novel_idea.angle: Start with the recurring Monday-morning failure: a team reaches an honest conclusion, but old prompts, permissions, dashboards, and commitments keep enforcing the rejected premise. End with a closing checklist that converts recognition into changed execution.
novel_idea.hook: The most dangerous Crossing is the one everyone agrees with and no system obeys.
novel_idea.argument_summary: A Crossing can successfully turn private recognition into common knowledge and still change nothing operationally. Once participants return to Run Time, existing doctrine, agent instructions, evaluations, permissions, workflows, metrics, and customer promises continue carrying the old map. AI makes this gap more dangerous because agents can faithfully execute stale doctrine at scale. Therefore, common knowledge is an intermediate result, not the completion criterion. Before closing the rite, the group must state what changed, identify where the revised doctrine will live, stop invalid workflows, update affected agents and commitments, and assign an owner for propagation. Otherwise Ritual Time produces insight while Run Time reproduces the error.
novel_idea.novelty_rationale: The closest prior post argues that a Crossing converts private truth into common knowledge without social rupture. This argument introduces a different endpoint and failure mechanism: common knowledge can exist while the organization continues executing the rejected premise through stale doctrine and automated workflows. The new operator decision is to withhold closure until the verdict has been propagated into the organization’s execution layer. That is not a narrower restatement of protected candor; it is a distinct bridge from Ritual Time to Run Time, made more consequential by machine agency.
novel_idea.source_grounding: Grounded in the source material’s Doctrine Reconstitution section, which says recognition remains vapor unless it is encoded into doctrine, agent instructions, evaluations, decision memory, permissions, workflows, and promises. It also draws on the stated loop from Ritual Time to revised doctrine to Run Time, and the warning that a lesson not encoded into doctrine becomes future incoherence.
